messages:
michael: paging SRE — prod-east preproc/tokenizer fleet is seeing repeated OOM kills and node CPU saturation. Multiple pods restarted in the last 5m. Customer-facing error spikes on text-gen routes. I'm paging oncall. :rotating_light:
incident-bot: INC-2026-045 created (sev2) — high error rate on /v1/generate due to preproc pod restarts. Pager sent to @sara oncall.
sara: I'm on it. Confirming which node pool, listing pods now. Any idea of traffic change?
michael: No config changes reported in the last hour. Traffic shows a big burst of very large prompts from a single customer ID (redacted) — looks like back-to-back long prompt ingestion.

Tom: grabbing logs and node metrics. Quick mitigation: can we scale preproc replicas + temporarily route traffic to dedicated pool?
sara: yes — start scale now and add a circuit-breaker to drop >120k chars. I'll coordinate routing with infra.

jess: pasted logs from preproc pod: ```
[2026-03-15T17:08:34Z] tokenizer_worker[pid=4231]: malloc(): out of memory
[2026-03-15T17:08:34Z] kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 4231 (tokenizer_worker) total-vm:2048328kB, anon-rss:1812300kB, file-rss:0kB
[2026-03-15T17:08:34Z] preproc[4231]: ERROR: failed to allocate buffer for tokenization
[2026-03-15T17:08:35Z] runtime: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY (occasionally seen on gpu-hosts when fallback path invoked)
```

michael: also seeing dmesg lines: "oom_reaper: reaped process 4231 (tokenizer_worker)". Node CPU is pegged at 98% while memory climbs then OOM.
tom: running `kubectl get pods -n prod | grep preproc` shows repeated CrashLoopBackOff on preproc-*/tokenizer pods. I'll cordon one suspect node and drain after we shift traffic.
sara: mitigation plan executing: 1) scale preproc replicas from 6 -> 12; 2) apply runtime toggle to disable naive full-document tokenization for requests >50k chars (reject with 413 for now); 3) cordon+drain two overloaded nodes; 4) temporarily route affected customer to dedicated backplane with rate limits.

jess: want to emphasize root cause hypothesis: recent change in prompt preprocessor (opens in last canary) introduced an O(n^2) path when normalizing nested lists which explodes memory on pathological inputs. I think it was rolled to canary -> prod rollout yesterday.
michael: can we rollback the preproc image to previous revision as a quick fix?
tom: yes, initiating rollout rollback on preproc deployment to image v2026.03.10-87. Applying: `kubectl set image deploy/preproc preproc=registry/redwood/preproc:v2026.03.10-87 -n prod`

deploy-bot: Rollout started for deployment/preproc namespace=prod by tom (rev back to v2026.03.10-87). Observability: canary -> full in 2m windows.
sara: after rollback, pods are coming up healthy on drained nodes. CPU usage falling to 45% on affected nodes. Restart count has stopped increasing. Error rate on /v1/generate dropped ~92% from peak.
michael: customer impact: a small fraction (~0.8%) of requests hit 5xx during the peak, with latency spikes for others. No long-term data loss. Notifying account team to reach out if needed.

jess: collecting traces and repro prompt to confirm the O(n^2) behavior. Will cut a small failing test and file bug. Postmortem owners: jess (eng-ml), tom (infra), sara (oncall/SRE).
sara: handing off incident to tom for post-rollback stabilization and follow-up. I'll update PD and mark as mitigated. Oncall handover note: I will be off at 18:10 UTC; tom takes postmortem lead.
tom: acknowledged. I'll keep the cordons for 30m, then re-evaluate. Next steps: pin preproc to old image, revert the naive normalization, add unit test for huge nested lists, add prompt-length rejects to runtime for safety.
michael: logging final mitigations and customer impact in the incident ticket. Good job team. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: INC-2026-045 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Participants: @sara (oncall), @tom (infra), @jess (eng-ml), @michael (pager).
notes: postmortem required; cause suspected O(n^2) prompt normalization; temporary mitigations: rollback, scale, circuit-breaker, node cordon/drain
